correctness.rationale: Write the nonzero rank-one N as uφ and apply the identity to inputs with φ=1: u² must be a scalar multiple of u. Reducedness ensures the scalar is nonzero, and each nonzero coordinate of u equals that scalar, so the image has a unique normalized generator e_S. Write N=e_S φ after rescaling and set c=φ(e_S). On the two orthogonal summands e_S A and (1−e_S)A the identity reduces to ψ(x)ψ(y)=cψ(xy) and η(x)η(y)=−cη(xy), respectively; the mixed equation is automatic. Setting x=y rules out c=0 because the target of each functional is a field. Thus ψ/c and, when nonzero, −η/c are unital characters. Orthogonal primitive idempotents show that a character selects one field factor, which must have degree one by injectivity on that factor. These conditions are also sufficient and give unique ordered inside/outside parameters even in characteristic two. For the labeled count the support is free on r−1 or r−2 indices after selecting the marked split factors. Equal-degree permutations act transitively at each fixed support-size pattern and respect the inside/outside roles; internal field automorphisms fix all displayed operators. At fixed c there are s split-support sizes in the first family and s−1 in the second, with independently r_d+1 choices for each higher degree. This includes the no-operator case s=0 and the r=1 split count q−1. Finally, N²=cN excludes nilpotence.
residual_risks: The proof is for k-linear rank exactly one on commutative finite étale algebras. The finite corroboration covers selected products and fields only.

value.rationale: The rank-one class is the smallest nonzero operator stratum on a natural class of semisimple commutative algebras. Its exact shape identifies which factors can detect an input, which can participate only in the output, and why no nonzero nilpotent rank-one operator exists there. The orbit count adds a complete classification up to algebra symmetries rather than a basis-dependent census or one small-instance table.
residual_risks: Nothing here classifies larger-rank operators or operators on nonreduced or noncommutative algebras.
